Senses.Explanation: When hunger comes, eat rice. Zen records turn the ordinary act into a compact answer, self-description, quotation, and point of public criticism, usually paired with sleeping when tired. Huanglong Huinan places it in a four-action series after contrasting ways of seeing a staff: eat when hungry, sleep when tired, approach fire when cold, and take coolness when hot (飢來喫飯，困來打睡，寒來向火，熱則取凉). Dahui Zonggao quotes Lingzhao's reply, neither hard nor easy—when hungry, eat rice; when tired, sleep (也不難也不易。飢來喫飯困來睡), and appraises the Pang family as walking together but not in step. Yuanwu Keqin uses the graphic variant ‘when hungry, eat rice’ (饑來喫飯) beside ordinary mind. Dongshan Zhiqian uses that variant in his own self-description, saying that he does not know how to discuss Chan or speak of the Way and only eats when hungry and sleeps when tired. Dazhu Huihai supplies the explicit contrast: other people refuse simply to eat or sleep and instead make a hundred demands and a thousand calculations. Hongzhi Zhengjue also refuses the line as a sufficient slogan: the monastery manager knows only eating when hungry and does not know the many kinds of affairs (只知飢來喫飯。且不知有許多般事). The ordinary meal is therefore bent into interview language, but the records themselves prevent merely repeating it from settling the matter.
Senses.Note: One action and one lexical sense were found. The contexts praise, quote, describe, or criticize its deployment; those different readings do not make eating into different things. The headword has 93 hits in 53 allowlisted texts. The common graphic variant, when hungry eat rice (饑來喫飯), is supporting family evidence and does not count toward the exact floor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 凡夫見拄杖，喚作拄杖；聲聞人見拄杖，認得箇頑空，撥無拄杖；菩薩人見拄杖，豈曾挂著齒牙？飢來喫飯，困來打睡，寒來向火，熱則取凉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要), in Huanglong Huinan's section, records Huanglong's exact four-action series after contrasting responses to a staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不如無事休歇去，飢來喫飯、睡來合眼，愚人笑我、智乃知焉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄): Linji Yixuan tells the assembly it is better to rest without affairs, eat rice when hungry, and close the eyes when sleepy.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我有一機，極盡玄微。飢來喫飯，寒來著衣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Xisou Shaotan (希叟紹曇禪師廣錄): in his own hall address Xisou says, 'I have one mechanism, exhausting the hidden subtlety: eat rice when hungry, put on clothes when cold.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 本覺者裡，但管飢來喫飯，困來打眠。熱則取凉，寒則向火。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liaoran Qingyu (了菴清欲禪師語錄): Liaoran tells the assembly that here one simply eats when hungry, sleeps when tired, takes coolness when hot, and approaches the fire when cold.

Occurrences.Kwic: 女子靈照云。也不難也不易。飢來喫飯困來睡。妙喜曰。此三人同行不同步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui Zonggao's Recorded Sayings (大慧普覺禪師語錄) records Lingzhao speaking the exact line and Dahui immediately appraising the three members of the Pang family as walking together but not in step.

Occurrences.Kwic: 院主只知飢來喫飯。且不知有許多般事。丹霞只知寒即向火。亦不知有許多般事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Hongzhi Zhengjue's Extensive Record (宏智禪師廣錄), Hongzhi uses the exact phrase while denying that the monastery manager's ordinary response exhausts the matter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以胸中無一事。飢來喫飯困來眠。雪竇意道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), Yuanwu Keqin places the exact line after having no affair in the breast, then resumes his account of Xuedou's point.

Occurrences.Kwic: 了取平常心是道。饑來喫飯困來眠。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄): Yuanwu Keqin uses the graphic variant ‘when hungry, eat rice’ (饑來喫飯) beside ordinary mind and sleeping when tired.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山不會談禪，不會說道，祇是饑來喫飯，困來打睡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Dongshan Zhiqian section: Dongshan says that he does not know how to discuss Chan or speak of the Way and only eats when hungry and sleeps when tired.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：飢來喫飯，困來即眠。曰：一切人總如是，同師用功否？師曰：不同。曰：何故不同？師曰：他喫飯時不肯喫飯，百種須索。睡時不肯睡，千般計校。所以不同也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Questions from Disciples in Every Quarter (諸方門人參問語錄), Dazhu Huihai dialogue: Dazhu says to eat when hungry and sleep when tired, then contrasts this with people who make a hundred demands at meals and a thousand calculations at bedtime.
